judge_claim: A hierarchical two-stage coefficient recovery strategy (learn single-mode coefficients first, then coupling coefficients) is proven to have covariance dominated by that of simultaneous estimation, Cov(delta g)_hierarchical <= Cov(delta g)_simultaneous, for all parameters (Section 4.1, Appendix A).

domain.single_mode_design: M1 with A=M1^dagger M1 positive definite
domain.coupling_design: M2 with D=M2^dagger M2 positive definite
domain.measurement_noise: independent, equal isotropic covariance in the two hierarchical stages and in the simultaneous comparison

exact_statement_tested: For every pair of design blocks satisfying the stated rank and noise assumptions, the full joint covariance difference Cov_sim-Cov_hier is positive semidefinite. In particular, both diagonal parameter blocks are dominated.
proof_obligation: Derive the complete hierarchical covariance, including cross-covariance, and certify Cov_sim-Cov_hier = Z Q^{-1} Z^dagger with Q=D-B^dagger A^{-1}B positive definite and Z=[A^{-1}B; -D^{-1}B^dagger A^{-1}B].
verdict_rule: VERIFIED only if the universal algebraic factorization is derived and its exact rational certificate and every predeclared numerical/control check pass; otherwise BLOCKED. A valid assumption-satisfying counterexample would be FALSIFIED.
scope_limit: The proof concerns the linear coefficient-recovery covariance model in Appendix A. It does not claim hardware noise is isotropic or that the independence assumption holds on a particular device.
